Weights reconverted from the 9.5 lb cock and 7.5 lb hen that Wikipedia and the Livestock Conservancy both give (the Livestock Conservancy says American Langshans are the Croad type): rooster 3.75 to 4.3 kg, hen 3 to 3.4 kg; the range-end alternatives dropped. Egg color shortened to dark brown. Egg size large added (Livestock Conservancy). Temperament list (which mixed in housing) replaced with calm, friendly, easily tamed. Heat tolerant yes added from the Livestock Conservancy (the only Asiatic breed suited to the Southern States). Eggs 140 to 150 and China origin confirmed.

Added egg size small from the Wikipedia egg weight of 30 to 35 g. Every field cited https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silkie, which is a disambiguation page with nothing about Showgirls, and the cached text is only a placeholder note. The record cited only the Cackle Hatchery home page, which says nothing about this bird. Added from Hoover's: 280 large eggs a year, temperament active, easy going, cold and heat hardy, broodiness low (rarely broody), pea comb. Cleared bantam_available (no source). Rewrote notable traits and history to match Hoover's. Hen and rooster weights left empty because Hoover's gives only a combined 5 to 6 lb. Only one publisher, and it is the seller, so it stays flagged.

Purpose dual-purpose (not a valid value and not right for a commercial laying hybrid) set to eggs: the Shaver line owner describes its brown hen as bred for high egg output, although Star Milling calls it dual purpose. Temperament list turned into quiet, calm. cold_hardy true turned into yes. Hen weight set to 2.9 kg from the Livestock Conservancy's 6.5 lb, with Wikipedia's 3.0 kg (7 lb) kept as a flagged alternative. Temperament written as calm, friendly (Livestock Conservancy). Confirmed with both Wikipedia and the Livestock Conservancy: 200 to 250 large light to dark brown eggs, low broodiness, rooster 3.9 kg (8.5 lb), rose comb, dual purpose, United States origin, cold and heat tolerance (Livestock Conservancy).

All filled fields match Wikipedia: large white eggs, hens usually non-sitting (low broodiness), meat purpose, French origin, four color varieties. Weights split into US and European standards instead of a pile of extraction values: rooster 3.6 kg and hen 2.9 kg from the Livestock Conservancy's 8 lb and 6.5 lb, with Wikipedia's European 3.0 kg and 2.5 kg (top of its 2.5 to 3 and 2 to 2.5 kg ranges) kept as flagged alternatives. Egg size kept large (Livestock Conservancy) with medium flagged, since Wikipedia gives an average egg of 53 g. Temperament list cut to calm, gentle, docile. Cold hardy no changed to partly: the Livestock Conservancy calls the breed of medium hardiness and Star Milling moderately hardy, with crests at risk of freezing when wet. White eggs, 140 to 230 eggs, dual purpose, crest, five toes and French origin confirmed by both Wikipedia and the Livestock Conservancy.

Possible duplicate of crevecoeur. The record had only white eggs, purpose and origin, so key facts were added from the Livestock Conservancy page: hen 6.5 lb (2.9 kg), rooster 8 lb (3.6 kg), 120 to 150 eggs a year, medium to large, moderately broody (medium), temperament gentle, docile, white skin, cold hardy partly (adapts to most climates but crests and beards can freeze when wet). White eggs, dual purpose, crest, v-shaped comb and French (Normandy) origin confirmed by both Wikipedia and the Livestock Conservancy; the Poultry Club of Great Britain also confirms the horn-type comb and French origin.

Weights were stored as min/max objects; set to numbers. Rooster 3.6 kg from the Livestock Conservancy's 8 lb, inside Wikipedia's 3.5 to 4 kg. Hen 2.9 kg from the Livestock Conservancy's 6.5 lb, with Wikipedia's European 3.0 kg (low end of 3 to 3.5 kg) kept as a flagged alternative. Eggs per year minimum 180 changed to 140: the Livestock Conservancy and Star Milling both give 140 to 220, and Wikipedia's 180 sits inside that. Egg size set to large to extra large (Livestock Conservancy and Star Milling agree). Temperament set to active, flighty (the Livestock Conservancy fact box and text). Heat tolerant yes added (Livestock Conservancy: prefers warm climates). White eggs, low broodiness, not cold hardy, dual purpose, v-shaped comb and French origin confirmed.

Hen weight set to 1.8 kg from the Livestock Conservancy's 4 lb (US standard), with the Poultry Club of Great Britain figure of 2.0 kg quoted by Wikipedia kept as a flagged alternative. Rooster 2.7 kg agreed by both (6 lb). Eggs per year set to 50 to 70 (Livestock Conservancy 50+, Wikipedia about 70) instead of a lone minimum of 70. Temperament list (which included a noise note) replaced with active, tame, friendly. White small eggs, non-sitters (low broodiness), ornamental purpose, poor cold tolerance, crest, v-shaped comb, feathered legs and Turkish origin confirmed by Wikipedia and the Livestock Conservancy; Star Milling's claim of large eggs and a dual-purpose role was not followed because both main sources disagree.

Eggs per year were a mix: the maximum of 120 was Wikipedia's figure for bantam hens, not large fowl. Set to 52 to 126 from the Livestock Conservancy (Wikipedia gives about 45 for standard hens, which sits just under that). Egg color yellowish-white set to cream to tinted, which matches the Livestock Conservancy text and is close to Wikipedia. Temperament list cut to docile, independent (the Livestock Conservancy fact box). Weights 2.5 kg and 1.8 kg (5.5 lb and 4 lb), small to medium eggs, broody hens, heat tolerance, exhibition purpose, five-point single comb and German origin confirmed by the Livestock Conservancy, Wikipedia and Star Milling.

All filled fields check out. Ornamental purpose, the three Japanese color varieties, non-molting tail and special hutches are confirmed by both Wikipedia and Star Milling; Japanese origin in Kochi Prefecture (Shikoku) in the 17th century and fancy use are also confirmed by the FAO DAD-IS Japan record. Single comb and white earlobes rest on Wikipedia only. No reliable source gives egg output, egg color or weights, so those stay empty.

Eggs per year set to 100 to 130 (Livestock Conservancy about 100, Wikipedia about 130) instead of a lone minimum of 130. Egg color set to white to tinted (Livestock Conservancy and Star Milling agree; Wikipedia says white or cream). Broodiness conflict settled at high: Wikipedia, Star Milling and the Poultry Club of Great Britain all call the hens excellent sitters, and the Livestock Conservancy also says they can be excellent mothers; the low alternative dropped. Temperament list cut to active, alert, flighty. cold_hardy yes cleared: the sources call the birds hardy and easy to raise but none says they handle cold. Weights 2.3 kg and 1.8 kg (5 lb and 4 lb), small eggs, ornamental purpose, pea comb and Indonesian origin confirmed.

Temperament was a list of five traits; replaced with the short phrase active, flighty, aggressive (Livestock Conservancy, Oklahoma State). Egg color tinted replaced with white or tinted, which Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State both give; the old alternatives were the same fact twice. Egg size set to small to medium per Livestock Conservancy. Purpose conflict dropped: exhibition is confirmed by Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State (ornamental only); fighting is history, not current use. Weights kept at the Livestock Conservancy typical 4 lb male and 3.5 lb female, with the Oklahoma State standard weights (5 lb cock, 4 lb hen) added as flagged alternatives. Egg count range kept as 40 (Wikipedia) to 160 (Livestock Conservancy), with the conflict on the low end kept because the sources really differ and output depends on strain.

Weights: main values changed from the British standard ranges to the US standard of 6 lb cock and 4.5 lb hen (2.7 and 2.0 kg), which Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State both give; the Wikipedia British ranges (3.2 to 4.1 kg cock, 2.25 to 3.2 kg hen) kept as flagged alternatives because the two standards really differ. Temperament was a list mixing growth and flock notes; replaced with calm, active, noisy (Livestock Conservancy, Oklahoma State says calm). Purpose conflict dropped: exhibition and ornamental mean the same here and Oklahoma State agrees it is a show bird. Heat tolerant added as yes: Livestock Conservancy says the breed prefers warm climates and does poorly in cold. Confirmed 50 to 80 small white eggs, cold hardy no, medium broodiness, England origin.

Egg color brownish or golden replaced with brown: Livestock Conservancy says brown and Oklahoma State says tinted brown. Egg max conflict dropped: Wikipedia's 80 falls inside the Livestock Conservancy range of 20 to 100, so it is not a real disagreement. Temperament was a list; replaced with active, quarrelsome, aggressive (Livestock Conservancy, Oklahoma State says rough with each other). Skin color yellow (legs) cleaned to yellow, which Oklahoma State gives as skin color. Weights of 9 lb cock and 7 lb hen (4.1 and 3.2 kg) confirmed by Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State. Purpose left as meat with exhibition as the flagged alternative, since Livestock Conservancy lists meat and Wikipedia says it is mostly shown. Cold hardy no and heat tolerant yes confirmed by Livestock Conservancy.

Rooster weight: the old 3.8 kg is a mean from one Indian study flock; main value changed to the US standard 6 lb (2.7 kg) from Oklahoma State, with 3.8 kg (Wikipedia) and 5.5 lb or 2.5 kg (Livestock Conservancy) kept as flagged alternatives. Hen weight 2.3 kg kept, now backed by Oklahoma State's 5 lb standard, with the Livestock Conservancy 4 lb (1.8 kg) as an alternative. Egg count: added a minimum of 6 and flagged the max, since Livestock Conservancy gives 6 to 40 eggs while Wikipedia gives about 70. Egg color cream to brownish changed to cream to light brown to match both Livestock Conservancy and Wikipedia. Added egg size small, temperament, heat tolerant yes and beginner friendly no from Livestock Conservancy. Skin color note removed; Oklahoma State gives white or yellow. Empty varieties filled from the four APA varieties Livestock Conservancy names.

Weights were wrong: 1.8 kg hen and 5.9 kg rooster came from the ends of Star Milling's 4 to 13 lb span across all Shamo sizes. Changed to the APA standard of 11 lb male and 7 lb female (5.0 and 3.2 kg), which Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State both give. Egg color brown narrowed to light brown and egg size medium to large added (Livestock Conservancy). Temperament added: friendly with people, aggressive to other chickens (Livestock Conservancy, Oklahoma State). Empty varieties filled with the three APA varieties both sources list. Origin Japan confirmed by all sources. Egg count left blank: sources give only a rough average of about 90.

Temperament was a list; replaced with the phrase tame, friendly, curious (Livestock Conservancy, Star Milling, Wikipedia). Hen and rooster weights now lead with the US standard from the Livestock Conservancy (4 lb = 1.8 kg hen, 6 lb = 2.7 kg cock), with the Wikipedia figures (1.6 kg and 2.4 kg) kept as a flagged alternative because the two standards really differ. Egg size kept small to medium (Livestock Conservancy) and the duplicate alternatives dropped. Purpose kept dual; the fighting and ornamental alternatives dropped since both sources describe a multi-purpose bird. Conservation status set to Critical, the value in the current Livestock Conservancy fact box; the Threatened value came from an older box on the same page. Egg color, egg count, heat tolerance, broodiness and origin confirmed.

Temperament was a list; replaced with lively, curious, friendly if handled young (Livestock Conservancy; Wikipedia agrees they are alert and trusting when raised calmly). Weights were the two ends of the Livestock Conservancy ranges shown as a conflict; hens are 3 to 3.5 lb and cocks 4.5 to 5.25 lb, so the midpoints 1.5 kg and 2.2 kg are used and the false conflict dropped. Purpose kept dual (Livestock Conservancy lists eggs and meat) with eggs kept as a flagged alternative, because Wikipedia says it is not a dual-purpose breed and the carcass is small. Empty varieties field cleared: it is a landrace with no fixed varieties. Egg color, egg size, egg count, broodiness, cold hardiness, beginner suitability and origin confirmed.

Egg size extra-large to large: Backyard Poultry gives an average of 2 oz (55 to 60 g), with only some hens laying extra-large eggs, and Skansen gives 45 to 70 g; the Star Milling value was the exception, not the rule. Temperament was a list; replaced with calm, friendly, independent (Skansen, Backyard Poultry, Star Milling). Added egg counts 150 to 175 a year (Skansen about 150, Backyard Poultry average 175), hen weight 2.3 kg and rooster 3.0 kg (both sources give hens 2 to 2.5 kg and cocks 2.5 to 3.5 kg; midpoints used), heat tolerant yes (Backyard Poultry: adapts well to hotter climates), broodiness medium (Skansen: tendency varies) and single comb (Backyard Poultry). Notable traits re-cited to Star Milling, which is where the largest Swedish breed, up to 8 lb, claim comes from. Egg color, cold hardiness, varieties, origin and status confirmed.

Temperament was a list; replaced with fairly docile, can be skittish (Star Milling says fairly docile, Wikipedia says a little skittish). Weights (7 lb cock, 6 lb hen), brown eggs, broodiness, single comb, red earlobes, sex-link crossing, dual purpose and origin all confirmed against Wikipedia, and purpose, temperament, broodiness and origin also against Star Milling. The Livestock Conservancy has no Iowa Blue page (404), and the other pages found were forums and content sites, so egg color and weights rest on Wikipedia alone and the breed stays in review. No source gives an egg count or egg size.

Temperament was a list and the Star Milling text it cites says nothing about temperament; replaced with docile, easy to handle from the Omlet breed page, which also says they forage well and like free range. History summary trimmed to what the sources say: the UK origin and the hardy claim are not stated in either source, so they were taken out of the text. Empty varieties field cleared. Egg count 250 to 270 (Star Milling only), dark chestnut brown often speckled eggs, strong shells, deep yellow yolks, egg purpose and the Rhode Island Red x Marans parentage confirmed against Star Milling and Omlet. Origin country United Kingdom left as it was but not confirmed by any source read, and no source gives weights, egg size or climate tolerance, so the record stays in review.

Wikipedia gives two sets of figures for eggs and weights; the FAO DAD-IS record for Bulgaria (Cherna shumenska kokoshka) matches the first set, so those are used and the conflicts dropped: 150 to 155 eggs a year, hen 1.5 kg (was 1.45), cock 1.9 kg (was 1.85). Egg color greyish-white to white, the DAD-IS shell color; Wikipedia's greyish-white is a shade of the same. Added egg size small (DAD-IS egg weight 46 g, Wikipedia 45 to 47 g in the same set). Empty varieties field cleared. Purpose eggs, single comb, white skin, origin, history and at risk status confirmed. No source describes temperament or climate tolerance.

Every filled field (large cream eggs, egg purpose, autosexing, Sweden, 1955, Martin Silverudd, the blonde head down on day-old males, the white males and spotted females) checks out against the Star Milling text. The only change is clearing the empty varieties field. Star Milling is the only publisher found; no second source could be checked (the session web search budget ran out), and no source gives egg counts, weights, temperament or climate tolerance, so the record stays in review.

Hen and rooster weights were stored as text ranges (2.0-2.5 and 2.0-3.0); set to numbers at the midpoints of the Wikipedia large fowl ranges, hen 2.3 kg and cock 2.5 kg. The FAO DAD-IS record for France gives 22.5 and 23 kg, plainly a decimal slip for about 2.3 kg, which fits. Earlobe color kept white (Wikipedia, citing the French standard) with blue kept as a flagged alternative, because the DAD-IS description says blue ear lobes. Large white eggs of at least 60 g, dual purpose, rose comb with a spike, the four colors, bantam, France, 1890s and at risk status confirmed. DAD-IS lists meat as the main use, which fits the dual-purpose value. Eggs and weights rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays in review.

Weights were stored as text ranges; set to numbers at the midpoints of the Wikipedia ranges, hen 2.0 kg (1.8 to 2.2) and cock 2.8 kg (2.5 to 3.0). The FAO DAD-IS record for Croatia (Stajerka) gives 1.7 and 2.5 kg, close enough to confirm. Egg count changed from 130 to 160 into 160 to 200: DAD-IS gives 160 to 200 and Star Milling 180 to 200, while Wikipedia gives 130 to 160 for the partridge type; the Wikipedia range is kept as a flagged alternative. Egg size small changed to medium, since Wikipedia gives a typical weight of 55 g, which is a US medium egg even though it calls them small; Star Milling's large kept as a flagged alternative. Egg color ivory changed to white to ivory (Wikipedia ivory, Star Milling white). Added broodiness low (Star Milling: rarely go broody). Dual purpose, single comb, white earlobes, varieties and origin confirmed.

Weights were stored as text ranges; set to numbers at the midpoints of the Wikipedia ranges, hen 2.1 kg (1.7 to 2.5) and cock 2.7 kg (2.3 to 3.1). Dual purpose, single buff color, single comb with five or six points, clean yellowish legs, hardiness, Portugal and not at risk status confirmed; the FAO DAD-IS record for Portugal also lists eggs and meat among its uses and gives not at risk. No source gives egg counts, egg color or size, or temperament, and weights rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays in review.

Added large fowl weights from the FAO DAD-IS record for Australia: hen 2.0 kg, cock 2.5 kg (the breeds.json weights are bantam figures, 765 g and 850 g, and were not used). Purpose kept as fighting and the duplicate fighting and ornamental alternatives dropped; Wikipedia says it was bred for cockfighting and may also be kept for ornament or the table. Brown eggs of medium to large size, single comb, the ten APA bantam colors plus brassy back and wheaten, United States origin and the Livestock Conservancy delisting confirmed against Wikipedia. Eggs rest on Wikipedia alone and weights on DAD-IS alone, and no source covers temperament or climate, so the record stays in review.

Weights were stored as text ranges; set to hen 1.7 kg and cock 2.2 kg, where the Wikipedia ranges (1.6 to 1.8 and 2.0 to 2.3 kg) and the FAO DAD-IS record for Switzerland (1.7 and 2.2 kg) agree; Omlet gives a little less (3.5 and 4.5 lb). Added eggs_per_year_min 100 (DAD-IS average) to go with the existing maximum of 150 (Wikipedia, first year). Added egg size medium to large (Wikipedia 55 g, Omlet large), temperament calm, docile, friendly, cold hardy yes and broodiness low, all from the Omlet breed page, which says the beard, rose comb and small wattles guard against frostbite. White eggs, rose comb, bantam, colors, Switzerland and the 1860s origin confirmed by Wikipedia, DAD-IS and the Poultry Club of Great Britain.

Added the missing key facts from the Livestock Conservancy page: 150 to 180 eggs a year (Wikipedia also gives about 150 in the first year), egg size medium to large (Wikipedia 55 g), temperament active, flighty, cold hardy yes, heat tolerant yes, broodiness medium (can go broody, excellent mothers) and purpose eggs. Weights added from the Livestock Conservancy US figures, hen 3.5 lb (1.6 kg) and cock 4.5 lb (2.0 kg), with the lighter European figures from FAO DAD-IS for Switzerland (1.3 and 1.7 kg, close to Wikipedia's just over 1 and 1.5 kg) kept as a flagged alternative. White eggs, V-comb, crest, colors, Switzerland, near extinction after the Second World War and revival confirmed by Wikipedia, the Livestock Conservancy, DAD-IS, Star Milling and the Poultry Club of Great Britain.

Added weights, which were missing from the extra record: cock 2.1 kg from the Wikipedia range of 1.75 to 2.5 kg, which the FAO DAD-IS record for France (2.2 kg) confirms; hen 1.6 kg from the Wikipedia range of 1.5 to 1.75 kg, with DAD-IS France's 1.85 kg (rounded 1.9) kept as a flagged alternative. Added eggs_per_year_min 140 (DAD-IS Belgium average) to go with Wikipedia's approximately 180, and egg size medium (Wikipedia average egg weight 52 g). Added purpose dual (Wikipedia infobox; DAD-IS lists meat as the main use). Varieties cleared: the stored value was a sentence saying twelve colors exist without naming any. White eggs, bantam, France and Belgium origin, 1882 description and history confirmed.

eggs_per_year_min was 120, which Wikipedia gives for bantam hens; set to 180, the large fowl figure that Wikipedia and the FAO DAD-IS record for Germany both give (max stays 180). Added egg size large (both sources give an average of 58 g). White eggs, dual purpose, cup or rose comb, white earlobes, black and blue-laced colors, bantam, Bavarian origin and endangered status confirmed.

Weights rounded to one decimal as the brief asks: hen 4.55 to 4.6 kg and cock 5.45 to 5.5 kg, the Australian Poultry Standard figures quoted by Wikipedia (breeds.json has a stray 4.75 kg for hens; Wikipedia's text says 4.55). Empty varieties field cleared. Origin, history and notable traits confirmed; the FAO DAD-IS record for Australia confirms it as a heavy, hard feathered breed at risk. No source gives eggs, temperament beyond tameness with its owner, or climate, and weights rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays in review.

History summary: corrected the misspelled Wakefer to Wakfer, as Wikipedia has it. Everything else checked out: brown eggs, egg and show purpose, hen 2.7 kg and cock 3.2 kg (Wikipedia infobox), black, blue and white varieties, bantam, single comb, white skin, feathered outer toe and Australian origin. Temperament cleared: the stored list (proud, aggressive-looking, alert, quick) is the standard's description of carriage and movement, not temperament, and no source describes temperament. Tinted egg color (Wikipedia infobox), fighting purpose, bantam, single or pea comb, Australian origin in the early 1900s and the 1936 and 1981 standards confirmed; the FAO DAD-IS record for Australia lists it as at risk. Everything rests on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays in review.

Egg color brown to light brown, the shell color in the FAO DAD-IS record for Malaysia (Wikipedia says brown; breeds.json says white and light brown). Weights rounded and checked: Wikipedia gives cocks 2.27 to 3.63 kg and hens 1.18 to 2.72 kg, so the midpoints 3.0 kg and 2.0 kg are used (were 2.95 and 1.95); the FAO DAD-IS record for Indonesia (Kedu) gives heavier birds, 3.6 and 3.0 kg, kept as flagged alternatives. Comb set to single, red or black (DAD-IS: thick, large, upright single comb, black or red). Varieties, black or white skin, Indonesian origin and history confirmed.

Added the facts the Wikipedia infobox carries but the extra record lacked: hen 1.5 kg and cock 2.5 kg (midpoints of 1 to 2 kg and 2 to 3 kg) and egg color white to light brown. Hen weight 3.6 to 3.5 kg, the FAO DAD-IS figure for France; cock 4.5 kg confirmed by DAD-IS and within Star Milling's 9 to 12 lb for adults.
