This is the Euskal Oiloa (Gallina Vasca). Purpose dual-purpose to dual (allowed value). Temperament changed from a list (friendly, hardy, good forager) to friendly; hardy and good forager are not temperament. Origin France/Spain to Spain: Wikipedia gives Spain as the country of origin and the breed standard is Spanish; Star Milling's France/Spain kept as a conflict alternative. Added hen 2.5 kg and rooster 3.6 kg from Wikipedia, with Star Milling's 9 lb (4.1 kg) rooster as an alternative. Confirmed 200 to 220 brown eggs a year (Wikipedia 209 to 220) and large size (Wikipedia about 60 g).

All filled fields match Wikipedia: 125 to 180 eggs a year, good sitters, 1.0 kg cock and 0.9 kg hen, single comb, white earlobes, Belgium, standard of 1930. Added egg_size small from Wikipedia's 42 to 48 g egg weight (US small grade). FAO DAD-IS (Belgium) confirms Belgian origin and egg use and describes it as a dwarf fowl related to the Brabanter, smaller and without crest. No second publisher gives weights or egg figures, so needs_review stays true.

All filled fields match Wikipedia: small white eggs, 0.65 kg cock and 0.55 kg hen, single comb, slate-blue legs, good sitters, Belgium, bred from about 1900 and standardised 1934. Added egg_size small from the 30 to 35 g egg weight. Caution: this record is the specific Belgian Bantam breed (Belgisch kriel, Naine belge), a relative of the Dutch Bantam. The Poultry Club of Great Britain Belgian page and similar hobby pages describe the bearded Belgian bantams (Barbu d'Anvers, d'Uccle and others), a different group, so they were not used as support. No second publisher found; needs_review stays true.

All filled fields match Wikipedia: about 130 white eggs a year, low broodiness, dual purpose, 3.25 kg cock and 2.25 kg hen (midpoints of 3 to 3.5 and 2 to 2.5 kg), single comb, white earlobes, Germany, standard of 1885, extremely endangered. Added egg_size medium from the 56 g average egg weight. FAO DAD-IS (Germany) confirms German origin, at-risk status and egg, meat and hobby use. The Poultry Club of Great Britain page could not be found (404) and search turned up only content farms, so needs_review stays true.

All filled fields match Wikipedia: about 150 white eggs a year, low broodiness, dual purpose, bantam exists, four colors, floppy single comb, Germany, known since the 18th century, extremely endangered. Added egg_size medium from the 55 g egg weight. Added hen 2.0 kg and rooster 2.4 kg, the midpoints of the Wikipedia infobox weights (1.75 to 2.25 kg and 2.0 to 2.75 kg) already stored in breeds.json. No linked DAD-IS record and no second publisher found, so needs_review stays true.

All filled fields match Wikipedia: about 180 white eggs a year, dual purpose, 2.6 kg cock and 2.05 kg hen (midpoints of 2.5 to 2.7 and 2.0 to 2.1 kg), yellow skin and earlobes, large single comb, Italy, recovery since 1999. Added egg_size medium from the roughly 50 g egg weight. FAO DAD-IS (Italy) confirms Italian origin, at-risk status and egg, meat and hobby use. No second publisher with egg or weight figures, so needs_review stays true.

Egg count conflict resolved at 230: the 160 alternative is Wikipedia's figure for bantam hens, not the large fowl; Star Milling also gives upwards of 230. Added egg_size large (Wikipedia about 60 g, Star Milling large) and temperament friendly (Star Milling). Brown eggs, Germany, 1970s, autosexing and dual purpose confirmed by both sources. Weights left empty: Star Milling's 10 to 12 lb rooster is a single hatchery-style figure with no hen weight and could not be checked against a standard (web search budget ran out).

All filled fields match Wikipedia: 180 to 200 pinkish brown eggs a year, dual purpose, 2.65 kg cock and 2.15 kg hen (midpoints of 2.5 to 2.8 and 2.0 to 2.3 kg), yellow skin, large single comb, Italy, standard of 2007. Added egg_size medium to large from the 55 to 60 g egg weight. FAO DAD-IS (Italy) confirms Italian origin, at-risk status and egg, meat and hobby use. No second publisher gives egg or weight figures, so needs_review stays true.

Egg count set to 160 to 200 (Livestock Conservancy); the old 165 minimum from Wikipedia and Star Milling falls inside that range. Added egg_size medium to large, hen 2.5 kg (5.5 lb), rooster 3.2 kg (7 lb), temperament active and broodiness low from the Livestock Conservancy. Wikipedia's 70 to 80 g eggs describe the Spanish Andaluza Azul population and were not used for size. Added heat_tolerant yes (Star Milling: light body and large comb suit warm climates; Livestock Conservancy: better suited to warm places) and cold_hardy partly (Livestock Conservancy: hardy even in cold, but better in warm climates). White eggs, Spain origin and egg purpose confirmed by three publishers. The conservation status alternatives are different countries, not a conflict, and were left as they are.

Cleared cold_hardy yes: Wikipedia only says the breed adapts to most conditions, which does not state cold hardiness. Added hen 2.5 kg, rooster 3.5 kg and egg_color creamy white from the Wikipedia infobox values already stored in breeds.json (3.5 kg, 2.5 kg, white cream). Confirmed up to 200 eggs a year, dual purpose and French origin. FAO DAD-IS (France) confirms French origin from a local breed crossed with Columbian Brahma at the end of the 19th century, lists meat as the main use and describes a semi-heavy, long-legged bird. No second publisher for egg or weight figures, so needs_review stays true.

Confirmed white eggs (Wikipedia, Star Milling), Netherlands origin (Wikipedia, Star Milling, Poultry Club of Great Britain), 170 eggs a year, 1.8 kg hen and 2.2 kg cock (midpoints of 1.6 to 2.0 and 1.9 to 2.5 kg), v-shaped comb, crest and bantam from 1934. Added egg_size medium from the 52 g average egg, temperament calm and cold_hardy yes from Star Milling (small comb and wattles resist frostbite). Note that FAO DAD-IS also lists a Belgian Brabanconne from the Belgian side of Brabant; the region straddles both countries. Weights, egg count and temperament rest on one publisher each, so needs_review stays true.

Possible duplicate of brakel (same Belgian breed; Braekel and Brakel are two spellings). Confirmed white eggs, Belgium, 2.0 kg hen and 2.25 kg cock (midpoints of 1.8 to 2.2 and 2 to 2.5 kg), gold and silver varieties, bantam version. Egg count widened to 180 to 200 (Wikipedia about 180, Star Milling 180 to 200). Added egg_size large (60 to 65 g), purpose eggs (Wikipedia and FAO DAD-IS Belgium, with Star Milling's dual purpose as a conflict alternative) and temperament active (Star Milling). Origin confirmed by the Poultry Club of Great Britain and DAD-IS. The conservation status alternatives are different countries, not a conflict.

Possible duplicate of braekel (same Belgian breed, two spellings). Temperament changed from a list (hardy, active, alert, good flier) to active: hardy and good flier are not temperament, and alert is not in the Star Milling text. Broodiness low cleared: Star Milling does not mention broodiness. Egg color white re-sourced to Wikipedia (Braekel article); Star Milling's 'silver or gold in color' describes the birds, not the eggs. Purpose dual-purpose to eggs (Wikipedia and FAO DAD-IS Belgium), with Star Milling's dual as a conflict alternative. Added hen 2.0 kg, rooster 2.25 kg and egg_size large from the Wikipedia Braekel article. 180 to 200 eggs a year and Belgian origin confirmed.

Cleared cold_hardy yes: Wikipedia says the birds resist disease and adverse environmental conditions, which does not state cold hardiness. Confirmed dual purpose, good sitters (broodiness high), 2.75 kg cock and 1.9 kg hen (midpoints of 2.3 to 3.2 and 1.5 to 2.3 kg), single comb, red earlobes, white plumage, naked neck, Portugal, not at risk in 2024. FAO DAD-IS (Portugal) confirms Portuguese origin, not-at-risk status and egg and meat use. No egg color, size or count is given by either source, and weights rest on Wikipedia alone, so needs_review stays true.

Temperament changed from a list (aggressive, powerful, hardy) to aggressive; powerful and hardy describe build and constitution, not temperament. Added hen 4.0 kg and rooster 5.25 kg (midpoint of 5.0 to 5.5 kg) from the Wikipedia infobox values already in breeds.json, and egg_size extra large from the 65 to 75 g egg weight. Confirmed about 150 cream eggs a year, poor sitters (broodiness low), fighting purpose, bantam version, triple comb, Belgium. FAO DAD-IS (Belgium) confirms Belgian origin and game fowl use. The conservation status alternatives cover large fowl and bantam separately, not a conflict. Egg and weight figures rest on Wikipedia alone, so needs_review stays true.

Egg color brown cleared: the Star Milling text never mentions eggs, and no other source gives an egg color. Purpose dual-purpose to dual (allowed value), now backed by Star Milling and the Poultry Club of Great Britain. Autosexing true to yes (the value style used elsewhere). United Kingdom origin confirmed by Star Milling (bred at Cambridge), the Poultry Club of Great Britain and FAO DAD-IS (UK, indigenous breed); standardised 1952 confirmed by both Star Milling and the Poultry Club. No source gives weights or egg figures, so needs_review stays true.

Confirmed origin (birds imported from Burma about 1880), single comb, small crest, white as the only recognised colour and true bantam status against the Poultry Club of Great Britain page, which agrees with Wikipedia. No egg, weight or temperament facts are published by either source, so none were added; the record stays flagged for review because the key facts are missing rather than wrong.

Possible duplicate of california-grey (same breed, UK spelling). Added egg_size large from Wikipedia, which says the breed was made to lay large white eggs; Star Milling says the same. Confirmed white eggs, dual purpose, autosexing, United States origin and 1930s date against Wikipedia and Star Milling. No reliable page gives egg counts, weights or temperament (hatchery and breed guide pages returned errors, the rest were content farms), so the record stays flagged.

Possible duplicate of california-gray (same breed, US spelling). Purpose dual-purpose to dual (value style). Autosexing true to yes (value style). Hen weight 2 kg to 1.8 kg: Star Milling gives birds as 4 to 6 pounds without splitting by sex, so the low end (4 lb) is used for hens and the high end (6 lb, 2.7 kg) kept for roosters. Temperament calm cleared: the cited Star Milling text says nothing about temperament. Removed the first name James from notable_traits and history_summary because Star Milling says James Dryden and Wikipedia says Horace Dryden; the family name is kept. Confirmed large white eggs and United States origin in the 1930s against both sources.

Temperament changed from a list of words to the phrase active, flighty, inquisitive (Livestock Conservancy, Wikipedia, Star Milling). Egg size kept at medium and the medium to large alternative dropped: Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State both say medium. Hen weight kept at 1.8 kg (4 lb, US standard in Livestock Conservancy and Oklahoma State) with the 2.3 kg British standard weight from Wikipedia shown as a conflict. Rooster weight 2.7 kg confirmed by all three. Added heat_tolerant yes because Livestock Conservancy says the breed prefers warmer climates. Confirmed 140 to 200 white eggs, low broodiness, cold_hardy no (does poorly in extreme cold; Oklahoma State notes it failed to adapt to harsh US conditions) and Belgian origin.

Rooster weight kept at 2.8 kg and the 3 kg alternative dropped: both come from the one Wikipedia range of 2.8 to 3 kg, so it is not a real conflict. Added egg_size large (Wikipedia gives an average egg of about 60 g; the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture breed catalogue says the eggs are large). Added broodiness low from the Ministry catalogue, which says hens almost never go broody except when old. Confirmed white eggs, egg purpose and Spanish origin against the Ministry catalogue. Egg count (200 to 225) and weights rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays flagged.

Temperament changed from a list to the phrase active, alert (Livestock Conservancy, Star Milling); Oklahoma State adds that the birds are wary of people and fly well. Egg size kept at medium to large and the medium alternative dropped: it came from an older sidebar on the same Livestock Conservancy page, and Star Milling also says medium/large. Conservation status kept at Critical, the current Livestock Conservancy status, and the old Watch sidebar value dropped. Confirmed 200 to 240 white to tinted eggs, hen 6 lb (2.7 kg) and rooster 8 lb (3.6 kg), low broodiness, heat tolerance and Spanish origin against Livestock Conservancy, Oklahoma State and Star Milling.

Confirmed about 150 cream eggs a year, good sitters (broodiness high), cuckoo as the only variety, single comb, clean pinkish-white legs, Belgian origin and critically endangered status against Wikipedia; FAO DAD-IS lists the breed in Belgium (Vlaanderse Koekoek) and France with egg use. Added egg_size large because Wikipedia gives an egg weight of about 60 g, which is large on the US scale. Added hen weight 2.5 kg and rooster weight 3.0 kg, the low ends of the Wikipedia infobox ranges (2.5 to 3.0 kg and 3.0 to 3.5 kg). No second publisher with breed facts could be reached, so the record stays flagged.

Possible duplicate of cr-vec-ur-chicken. Purpose dual-purpose to dual and crest true to yes (value styles). The record had only white eggs and origin, so key facts were added from the Livestock Conservancy page and confirmed by Oklahoma State: hen 6.5 lb (2.9 kg), rooster 8 lb (3.6 kg), 120 to 150 white to tinted eggs a year, medium to large, moderately broody, gentle and docile. Added a v-shaped comb, white skin and the black, blue and white varieties (Oklahoma State). Confirmed French origin (Normandy) against Wikipedia, Livestock Conservancy, Oklahoma State and the Poultry Club of Great Britain.

Confirmed 160 eggs a year, single red comb, Bohemian origin with a first record in 1205, endangered status and the plumage traits against Wikipedia. Added egg_size medium to large because Wikipedia gives eggs of 55 to 60 g, which spans medium and large on the US scale. Added hen weight 2.0 kg and rooster weight 2.3 kg, the low ends of the Wikipedia infobox ranges (hens 2.0 to 2.5 kg, cocks 2.3 to 2.8 kg). No DAD-IS record is linked and no second publisher could be reached, so the record stays flagged.

Broodiness 'yes, willing to go broody' to medium (value style; Star Milling says only that hens are willing to go broody). Purpose dual-purpose to dual and crest true to yes (value styles). Added egg_size large from Star Milling, which says hens lay large white eggs. Confirmed white eggs, French origin, 1996 creation from Gournay and Crevecoeur stock and the mottled crested look against Star Milling. Star Milling is the only source; no Wikipedia page is cached and a French Wikipedia lookup failed, so weights, egg counts and temperament are unknown and the record stays flagged.

The Deathlayer is the German Westfaelischer Totleger; its English Wikipedia page was used as a second source. Temperament cleared: the old value was a habit (roosting in trees), and no source describes temperament. Notable traits rewritten: Star Milling's black plumage with a cushion comb does not match Wikipedia, which gives gold-pencilled and silver-pencilled colours and a rose comb, and Wikipedia says the lay-until-death story is not where the name comes from (it grew out of Alltagsleger, daily layer, through Low German). History summary corrected to match. Added eggs about 180 a year, broodiness low (non-sitters), comb rose, varieties gold-pencilled and silver-pencilled, hen 1.5 kg and rooster 2.0 kg (low ends of the 1.5 to 2 and 2 to 2.5 kg ranges), all from Wikipedia. Confirmed white eggs, medium size (eggs 50 to 65 g) and German origin in both sources.

Every filled field (fighting purpose of the original gamecock strain, white earlobes in the University of Delaware flock, Delaware origin, name dating from 1775, state bird status, Blue Andalusian crossing) matches Wikipedia. The Livestock Conservancy page cached for this record is about the Delaware chicken, a different breed, and was not used; its facts must not be copied here. The Blue Hen is a strain rather than a recognised breed, and no source gives egg, weight or temperament facts, so the record stays flagged.

Purpose ornamental to dual: Wikipedia never calls the breed ornamental, and the FAO DAD-IS record for Turkey lists eggs, meat and fancy as its uses (the breeds.json row also says multipurpose). Confirmed Turkish origin, the long crow of 20 to 25 seconds, the plumage and leg colours and the conservation programme against Wikipedia; DAD-IS confirms Turkish indigenous origin and at-risk status. Wikipedia gives a weight of 3 to 3.5 kg without saying which sex, so no hen or rooster weight was added. No egg or temperament facts are published, so the record stays flagged.

Temperament changed from a list to the phrase active, alert (Livestock Conservancy breed facts); the page adds that birds can be shy and somewhat wild. Hen weight 2.75 to 2.7 kg and the conflict dropped: Livestock Conservancy's 6 lb is 2.7 kg and Wikipedia's 2.75 kg is the same weight rounded differently. Conservation status merged into one value, because the RBST Vulnerable rating (UK) and the Livestock Conservancy Critical rating (US) are two different lists, not a conflict. Confirmed 150 to 200 white eggs (Livestock Conservancy, Star Milling), medium to large size, rooster 7.5 lb (3.4 kg), low broodiness, cold hardy but not heat hardy, dual purpose and Derbyshire origin (Livestock Conservancy, Wikipedia, Poultry Club of Great Britain).

Confirmed meat purpose, Vietnamese origin, the enlarged legs and feet, the incubation problem and the slaughter weight of 3 to 5 kg against Wikipedia; the FAO DAD-IS record for Viet Nam agrees on meat and fancy use, origin in Hung Yen Province (where Khoai Chau District lies) and very big shanks. Rooster weight 6 kg is kept but it is the upper figure Wikipedia says males can reach, not a standard weight. No egg or temperament facts are published, so the record stays flagged.

Temperament changed from a list to the phrase friendly, somewhat flighty (Wikipedia; Star Milling also says friendly). Added egg_size small: Wikipedia and Star Milling both say the eggs are small. Confirmed about 160 cream or white eggs a year (Wikipedia, Star Milling), true bantam weights of up to 550 g for cocks and 450 g for hens (Star Milling gives about 15 oz), easy broodiness, not especially cold hardy, Dutch origin and the 13 UK colours (Poultry Club of Great Britain). Weights left at two decimals because this is a true bantam and rounding would distort them.

heat_tolerant changed from boolean true to "yes" to match the value style (Star Milling). Added eggs_per_year_min 160 and eggs_per_year_max 220 and egg_size large: Catalan Wikipedia gives about 160 eggs a year (220 in improved lines) at about 60 g, and Agraria.org gives 180 eggs of 60 g with reddish shells. Egg color, origin Spain and egg purpose confirmed. Weights conflict: Agraria.org (Spanish standard) gives 3.45 kg cock and 2.5 kg hen, and Catalan Wikipedia calls it a semi-heavy type, while Star Milling gives about 5 to 6 lb and 4 lb; main values set to 3.5 and 2.5 kg with the Star Milling figures kept as alternatives.

Hen and rooster weights: the old alternatives were only the two ends of the Wikipedia range, not a real conflict. Wikipedia gives 3.4 to 3.9 kg cocks and 2.6 to 3.1 kg hens; Agraria.org gives 3.0 to 3.5 kg and 2.2 to 2.6 kg. Kept 3.4 kg and 2.6 kg, which fall inside both ranges, and dropped the alternatives. Added egg_size medium to large (both sources give 55 to 60 g). Confirmed 170 to 190 eggs a year, pinkish shell, dual purpose, Italy, single comb, red lobes and yellow skin with Agraria.org.

Added purpose meat from the FAO DAD-IS record for France, which lists meat as the breed's use. Confirmed French origin (Estaires, Nord-Pas-de-Calais), the small serrated comb, slightly feathered dark legs and the black, gold-necked and silver-necked plumage against Wikipedia; DAD-IS also records slightly feathered shanks. DAD-IS adds that the breed died out after the Second World War, was re-created by northern breeders, and descends from local fowl, the Combattant du Nord and the Langshan, while Wikipedia calls it a Langshan variety; both are kept out of the key facts. The Wikipedia infobox gives 2.2 kg for both sexes, which looks unreliable, so no weights were added. No egg or temperament facts are published, so the record stays flagged.

origin_country shortened from "Spain (Basque Country) and south-western France" to "Spain": the breed standard is Spanish and the whole 2013 population was in the Spanish Basque Country. Added egg_size large (eggs about 60 g). Weights 3.6 kg cock and 2.5 kg hen, brown eggs, five varieties, yellow skin and legs confirmed by Agraria.org, but its breed page is largely a translation of the Wikipedia article, so it is not a fully independent check; egg numbers (209 to 220) rest on Wikipedia alone. Left in review.

Temperament was a list of traits (hardy, vocal when handled, strong flier), not a temperament; replaced with "flighty, lively" from Omlet, which describes lively, very flighty birds that never fully tame, matching the Poultry Club note on strong fliers that are vocal when handled. Added missing weights: hen 1.4 kg (3 lb) and rooster 1.8 kg (4 lb) from Omlet; Agraria.org gives a close 1.6 and 2.0 kg. Confirmed small white or cream eggs (Star Milling says off white), heat tolerance (Wikipedia, Star Milling), low broodiness (Wikipedia, Omlet), egg purpose and Egypt origin.

Temperament was a list of traits (active, hardy, flighty, not docile); replaced with "active, flighty" (Star Milling, Poultry Club of Great Britain). Weights: the old alternatives were only the ends of the Wikipedia ranges (cocks 1.4 to 1.6 kg, hens 1.2 to 1.4 kg); Agraria.org gives 1.5 to 1.6 kg and 1.2 to 1.3 kg, so set rooster 1.5 kg and hen 1.3 kg, which sit inside both, and dropped the alternatives. Eggs per year: Wikipedia says about 200 and Star Milling 150 to 180, so the range is now 150 to 200. Added egg_size small to medium (Star Milling says small; Wikipedia and the Italian standard give about 52 g). White eggs, white earlobes, low broodiness and Netherlands origin confirmed.

Purpose dual-purpose to dual (house style). Hen weight 1.8 to 2.0 kg: Agraria.org gives 2.0 to 2.1 kg hens and 2.5 to 2.7 kg cocks, which also sits inside Star Milling's 4 to 6 lb range; rooster 2.7 kg confirmed. Confirmed about 180 white eggs a year, Piedmont (Italy) origin and the 1999 recovery from both publishers.

Added hen weight 3.0 kg (Poultrykeeper gives hens 2.5 to 3.5 kg and cocks 3 to 4.5 kg, matching the Wikipedia infobox range); rooster 4 kg confirmed. Added 150 to 200 eggs a year from Poultrykeeper. Egg color left as cream (Wikipedia) but flagged as a conflict with brown (Poultrykeeper). Origin Germany confirmed by the Poultry Club of Great Britain (imports of Croad stock in 1879, breed club 1895). Temperament has only the Wikipedia line that the birds tame easily.

All filled fields match the Wikipedia text: 180 to 190 brown eggs a year, hens about 3 kg and cocks about 4 kg at six months, dual purpose, India. The FAO DAD-IS India record confirms it is a crossbreed developed for rural poultry. No second publisher with egg or weight figures could be read (indiafarm.org returned 403, the Assam government PDF did not parse), so needs_review stays true.

Purpose dual-purpose to dual (house style). Broodiness 'yes' cleared: Star Milling only says hens will go broody, which gives no low, medium or high level. Added egg size extra large: Star Milling says extra large white eggs and the French standard (French Wikipedia) asks for hatching eggs of at least 65 g with white shells. Weights confirmed: the standard minimums are 2.5 kg cock and 2 kg hen, consistent with 2.3 kg hen and Star Milling's 4 to 7 lb range. Normandy origin confirmed by FAO DAD-IS and French Wikipedia.

Existing fields (dual purpose, Poland, 1879 description, 1923 recognition, conservation flocks) confirmed against English Wikipedia and the FAO DAD-IS Polish records. Added weights and egg numbers from Polish Wikipedia: cocks 2.2 to 2.7 kg (set 2.5), hens 1.8 to 2.3 kg (set 2.1), 140 to 180 eggs a year. Polish Wikipedia notes the 1879 date may really be 1899. Egg color not filled: no source read states it. Only Wikipedia gives the weights and egg counts (agrofakty.pl read but it looks like generated content and was not relied on), so needs_review stays true.

Origin Vietnam (Bac Ninh Province) confirmed by English Wikipedia and the FAO DAD-IS Viet Nam record. Added weights from Vietnamese Wikipedia: cocks 4.5 to 5.5 kg (set 5.0), hens 3.5 to 4.0 kg (set 3.8). Added purpose meat from FAO DAD-IS (uses: hobby, meat). No source read gives egg numbers, egg color or temperament. Weights rest on one publisher, so needs_review stays true.

Purpose dual-purpose to dual (house style). Egg size medium to medium to large (Livestock Conservancy says medium to large and large; Wikipedia says medium). Added 200 to 240 eggs a year, temperament calm and cold hardy yes from the Livestock Conservancy (winter hardy, fairly cold tolerant, calm); Star Milling also says calm. Weights kept at the APA standard from Wikipedia (8.5 lb cock, 6.5 lb hen) but flagged as conflicts, because the Livestock Conservancy breed facts give 6 lb male and 4 lb female. White eggs, US origin (Rutgers, APA 1949) confirmed by both.

Origin Croatia and 1917 development confirmed by Wikipedia and the FAO DAD-IS Croatia record. Added from FAO DAD-IS: cocks 3.5 to 4 kg (set 3.8), hens 2.5 to 3 kg (set 2.8), more than 200 eggs a year with good care (eggs_per_year_min 200), purpose dual (uses eggs and meat), broodiness high (the record says the hens kept the instinct to sit and care well for chicks). No source read gives egg color, egg size or temperament. Guessed Croatian Wikipedia URLs returned 404. Key facts rest on FAO alone, so needs_review stays true.

Eggs per year max 80 kept and the 160 alternative dropped: the Livestock Conservancy says fewer than 160, which does not contradict Wikipedia's about 80. Temperament list (mixed in flock notes) replaced with calm, docile (Livestock Conservancy). Purpose set to plain meat (Livestock Conservancy, FAO DAD-IS UK record, Wikipedia). Egg color light brown / tinted to light brown (Wikipedia light brown, Livestock Conservancy cream or light brown). Added egg size small to medium (Wikipedia small, Livestock Conservancy small to medium). Added cold hardy no and heat tolerant no: Wikipedia says the thin, downless feathers leave it open to cold, and the Livestock Conservancy says it does poorly in very cold or hot weather. Weights 4.8 kg and 3.6 kg (10.5 lb and 8 lb) confirmed from the Livestock Conservancy. Origin Cornwall, England confirmed by the Poultry Club of Great Britain and FAO.

Eggs per year 270 to 160 to 200: the 270 was extrapolated from a Roslin study laying rate of 0.74 eggs a day, not an annual figure; Poultrykeeper gives 160 to 200 tinted eggs. Hen weight 4.03 to 3.2 kg: 4.03 was one study group's live weight at 55 weeks, not the breed standard; Poultrykeeper gives cock 4.1 kg and hen 3.2 kg, so rooster weight 4.1 kg was added. Temperament alert, active added (Poultrykeeper). Tinted eggs, pea comb, white skin and Suffolk, England origin (Appleyard, 1932) confirmed by Wikipedia, Star Milling, the Poultry Club of Great Britain and Poultrykeeper; cold hardy confirmed by Star Milling.

All filled fields match the Wikipedia text: about 215 white eggs a year (minimum 55 g), egg purpose, autosexing, single comb, two color varieties, bantam approved 1994, Norway origin and the Bryne breeding station history. The breeds.json infobox weight of about 1.7 kg for both sexes was not copied in, because the cached text does not state it and a cock the same weight as a hen needs checking. Norwegian Wikipedia was read but is tagged as fully unsourced, so it was not used. No second publisher found, so needs_review stays true.

All filled fields match the Wikipedia text: Korea, origin estimated in the mid third century, tails up to 1.5 m, annual tail molt unlike the Onagadori, near loss in the early 1900s, about 250 birds in conservation in 2021. Purpose ornamental is not stated in English Wikipedia but Korean Wikipedia describes long-tailed chickens as pet (ornamental) breeds, so it was kept. No source read gives eggs, weights, egg color or temperament. Korean Wikipedia is a short unsourced stub, and no second publisher was found, so needs_review stays true.

Removed 'hens can crow like roosters' from notable traits and history summary: it rests on one garbled Wikipedia sentence that confuses the breed's long, stepped cock crow with hen crowing, and the FAO DAD-IS record says nothing of it. Kept the long crow of up to 60 seconds, golden sickles, yellow shanks and single comb (FAO adds that some birds have rose combs and that shanks range from white through yellow to black). West Sumatra origin confirmed by FAO (Solok). Purpose ornamental kept: FAO lists fancy and hobby uses alongside eggs, meat and research. No source read gives eggs, weights or egg color, so needs_review stays true.

Weight conflicts removed: the alternatives were only the two ends of Wikipedia's ranges, not a disagreement. Hen weight set to 1.8 kg (range 1.5 to 2 kg) and rooster to 2.6 kg (range 2 to 3.25 kg), midpoints of the stated ranges. Added egg size medium to large from the stated 55 to 60 g egg weight. Confirmed 160 white eggs a year, non-sitting hens (broodiness low), black plumage, crest, V comb, Kosovo origin and the 20 to 60 second crow. A guessed German Wikipedia URL returned 404 and no second publisher was found, so needs_review stays true.

Weights were stored as min/max objects, not numbers. Hen weight set to 1.8 kg (English and German Wikipedia: 1.5 to 2.0 kg) and rooster weight to 2.0 kg (German Wikipedia infobox 1.75 to 2.25 kg; English Wikipedia gives a 2.25 kg maximum). Added about 180 eggs a year from German Wikipedia. Added purpose dual from FAO DAD-IS (uses eggs, meat, hobby). White eggs, single comb, white earlobes, Germany (Bergisches Land and Westphalia) confirmed by English and German Wikipedia and FAO. Egg numbers and weights rest on Wikipedia only, so needs_review stays true.

Purpose set to plain eggs; the exhibition alternative dropped (Wikipedia says kept as a layer or show bird, Poultrykeeper lists eggs). Rooster weight 2.75 rounded to 2.8 kg (Wikipedia 2.75 kg, inside Poultrykeeper's 2.5 to 2.95 kg); hen 1.8 kg confirmed (Poultrykeeper 1.8 to 2.5 kg). Added 150 to 180 eggs a year, temperament active, good-natured and cold hardy yes from Poultrykeeper (hardy, lays even in cold weather). Broodiness high cleared: both sources only say hens will go broody, with no level given. Off-white eggs and German-Dutch border origin confirmed by both.

All filled fields match the Wikipedia text: developed from 1912 by Harry S. Lamon at the USDA Beltsville station from white Plymouth Rock, silver-gray Dorking and white Leghorn; APA 1933, bantam 1960; white plumage, yellow skin, single comb, red earlobes; white eggs; dual purpose (layer that still gives a tender carcass); the Livestock Conservancy could find no original stock in 2013. The guessed Livestock Conservancy breed page returned 404, and no source gives egg numbers or weights. Single publisher, so needs_review stays true.

Comb value was inverted: English Wikipedia says single combs have NOT been allowed since 2000, and the French standard (French Wikipedia) gives a triple (pea-type) comb, so comb changed to triple. Added weights from the French standard: cock minimum 4 kg with 5 kg desired (set 5.0), hen minimum 3.5 kg (set 3.5). Added egg color tinted (standard: lightly tinted shell, hatching eggs 60 to 65 g). Belgium origin, late 1800s, fighting purpose, bantam form and slate-blue legs confirmed. Weights and egg color rest on Wikipedia only, so needs_review stays true.

Purpose dual-purpose to ornamental: nothing in the cited Star Milling text supports dual purpose, and FAO DAD-IS lists the only use as fancy. Temperament trimmed to docile, quiet, friendly ('good forager' is not temperament). Notable traits: removed 'produces excellent white meat' and 'flat-feathered and frizzled forms both exist', which are not in the cited text; added frizzled plumage from FAO DAD-IS. Added egg size medium (Star Milling; French standard asks for hatching eggs of at least 55 g). Added weights from the French standard: cock 2.5 kg, hen 1.5 kg. White eggs (French standard: white to cream), Lyon, France origin and Tamburini as creator confirmed by Star Milling, FAO and French Wikipedia; FAO gives approval in 1969. Crest kept from Star Milling but the French standard lists no crest, so it needs a check. Weights rest on one publisher, so needs_review stays true.

All existing fields match English Wikipedia (140 to 160 tinted eggs of about 65 g, excellent sitters, meat purpose, usually single comb, lightly feathered legs, Mechelen origin from about 1852). Meat purpose, Belgian origin and feathered legs also confirmed by FAO DAD-IS. Added weights: English Wikipedia infobox gives cock 5 kg and hen 4 to 4.5 kg, French Wikipedia's standard gives cock 4 to 5 kg and hen 3 to 4 kg; set rooster 5.0 kg and hen 4.0 kg, the value both ranges share. Egg color kept as tinted but flagged, because the French standard gives brown shells. Guessed Poultrykeeper and Poultry Club URLs returned 404, so weights and eggs rest on Wikipedia only and needs_review stays true.

Temperament list (mixed in 'can fly') replaced with calm but active, flighty (Wikipedia: generally calm, active, can fly, known for being flighty). Egg color conflict dropped: tinted (Wikipedia, Poultrykeeper) and cream (Star Milling) describe the same shell. Weights were the standard maximums (2.95 kg cock, 2.5 kg hen); Poultrykeeper gives cock 2.5 to 2.95 kg and hen 2.0 to 2.5 kg, so set rooster 2.7 kg and hen 2.3 kg. Eggs set to 160 to 210 a year from Poultrykeeper, consistent with Star Milling's about 200. Rose comb, white earlobes, green legs, no bantam, egg-laying purpose and Southport, Lancashire origin confirmed by Wikipedia, Poultrykeeper, Star Milling and FAO DAD-IS.

Confirmed weights (cock 0.7 to 0.8 kg, hen 0.6 to 0.7 kg), egg color and origin against FAO DAD-IS (male 0.75 kg, female 0.7 kg, light brown shell). Added eggs per year 120 to 170 and egg size small (35 g eggs) from DAD-IS; Wikipedia also gives 35 g. Skin color left as yellow per Wikipedia; DAD-IS lists white skin, so that field is not confirmed.

Confirmed origin (United Kingdom), purpose (ornamental), lightly feathered legs, history and conservation status against Wikipedia, the Poultry Club of Great Britain and FAO DAD-IS (indigenous UK breed, 40 to 100 birds in 2002). No egg count, egg size, weight or temperament is filled, and no source found gives them for this breed, so nothing was added. The Livestock Conservancy Langshan page says the Modern type lost its leg feathering, which disagrees with Wikipedia's lightly feathered legs; left as partly.

Temperament was a list with a behavior note in it; set to the short phrase active, lively (Wikipedia; Agraria.org says very lively and always moving, though docile). Confirmed weights (cock 0.8 kg, hen 0.7 kg), Tuscan origin, true bantam status and strong broodiness against Agraria.org, which prints the draft Italian standard. FAO DAD-IS confirms Italy and egg plus meat use. Egg color (ivory white) and heat and cold hardiness rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays flagged for review.

Temperament list replaced with the phrase calm, friendly (Livestock Conservancy, Star Milling). Purpose conflict settled at exhibition: Wikipedia says it is kept mainly for fancy and exhibition, and the Livestock Conservancy's eggs and broody use is covered by the egg and broodiness fields; the eggs alternative dropped. Added cold_hardy partly, because the Livestock Conservancy says the single comb is prone to frostbite and the breed is not the best choice for northern climates. Confirmed weights 24 oz male (0.68 kg) and 22 oz female (0.62 kg) with the Livestock Conservancy and Star Milling, and 80 to 100 small creamy white eggs a year.

Temperament list replaced with docile (the flying note is behavior, not temperament). Added large fowl weights from TierWelt's breed profile: cock 3.5 to 4 kg, hen 2.5 to 3 kg. Added egg size medium (55 g eggs per Wikipedia and TierWelt). Purpose set to dual with meat kept as a conflicting alternative: Wikipedia says it was bred as a meat chicken, TierWelt calls it a dual purpose bird laying about 200 eggs a year. Confirmed 200 eggs a year and cream to light brown shells with both sources, and German origin with FAO DAD-IS.

Temperament cleared: the value was good forager, which is a habit, and no source describes the bird's temperament. cold_hardy cleared: Wikipedia only says hens keep laying through winter, which is not a statement about cold hardiness, and no other source covers it. Confirmed 150 to 220 pale brown (tinted) eggs a year, cock 7 to 8 lb (3.2 to 3.6 kg) and hen 5 to 6 lb (2.25 to 2.7 kg) with Star Milling, and origin near Norwich with the Poultry Club of Great Britain and FAO DAD-IS.

Temperament list turned into the phrase quiet, docile (Wikipedia). Added egg color tinted from the Rare Poultry Society breed page. Added large fowl weights from the Wikipedia infobox (cock 3.5 to 4 kg, hen 2.75 to 3.25 kg); no second publisher found for them, and the 180 to 240 eggs a year also rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays flagged. Confirmed Dutch origin about 1900 and meat use with FAO DAD-IS, and lightly feathered shanks in the British standard with the Poultry Club of Great Britain and the Rare Poultry Society.

Egg color white to light tinted changed to white: the live Wikipedia article says the eggs are white, with a minimum weight of 55 g. Temperament cleared: hardy, active, good flier appears in no source, and the value mixed hardiness and flying with temperament. Added weights from FAO DAD-IS (Norsk jaerhona): cock 2.5 kg, hen 1.5 kg. Wikipedia's infobox gives about 1.7 kg for both sexes, kept as a conflicting alternative for the cock; the identical hen figure looks like a copy error and was not used. Added eggs_per_year_max 215 so the range matches the 215 eggs a year both sources give. Confirmed Norwegian origin, egg use and autosexing with DAD-IS.

Confirmed origin in Kochi Prefecture on Shikoku, descent from long-tailed breeds crossed with Chabo type bantams, the dragging tail of old cocks, true bantam status and UK breeding from the 1990s against the Poultry Club of Great Britain. The Poultry Club dates it to the mid nineteenth century, which falls inside Wikipedia's Edo period, so no change. FAO DAD-IS lists the breed in Germany and the UK; the Japanese DAD-IS record that names Ohiki as an alias describes the Minohiki-chabo (natural monument 1967), so its weights were not used. No egg, weight or temperament data found from any source, so those fields stay empty and the record stays flagged.

Temperament cleared: the value hardy describes toughness, not temperament, and no source describes temperament. Added weights from the Wikipedia infobox, cock 2.7 to 3.2 kg and hen 2.25 to 2.7 kg; FAO DAD-IS (UK) gives 2.9 kg and 2.3 kg, inside those ranges. Confirmed origin in Yorkshire, the 1914 naming, the older names and dual utility use with the Poultry Club of Great Britain and DAD-IS. White eggs rest on Wikipedia alone; DAD-IS gives about 160 eggs a year as an average only, so no range was added.

Temperament list turned into the phrase calm, friendly (Livestock Conservancy: calm and friendly, though not docile; Wikipedia and Star Milling: relatively calm). Added egg size small to medium and about 100 eggs a year (eggs_per_year_max 100) from the Livestock Conservancy. Rooster weight kept at 3.6 kg (Wikipedia) with the Livestock Conservancy's 8.5 lb (3.9 kg) as a conflicting alternative; hen 3 kg matches its 6.5 lb (2.9 kg). Confirmed light brown eggs, low broodiness, cold hardiness, meat use and Persian (Gilan, Iran) origin with the Livestock Conservancy, Star Milling and the Poultry Club of Great Britain.

Added weights from FAO DAD-IS (Orusthona): cock 2 kg, hen 1.4 kg. The first notable trait and the history summary said the breed came from an island and was extremely rare; Star Milling only says the west coast of Sweden and gives no rarity claim, so both were rewritten to match the source. DAD-IS confirms Swedish origin as a native local population, egg use, about 150 eggs a year on average and an at risk status with 520 birds in 2023. White, small to medium eggs rest on Star Milling alone, so the record stays flagged.

Weights widened from single maximums to the full ranges in the Wikipedia infobox: cock 2.25 to 3 kg, hen 1.75 to 2.5 kg; FAO DAD-IS gives 2.75 kg and 2.2 kg, inside those ranges. Added egg color white and egg size medium (55 g eggs) from DAD-IS, purpose dual (DAD-IS lists eggs and meat), and bantam_available yes (DAD-IS has a separate Ostfriesische Zwerg-Mowen record). Confirmed about 170 eggs a year and north-west German origin with DAD-IS.

Confirmed 160 to 180 eggs a year, pinkish eggs of 40 to 45 g, cock 1.3 to 1.5 kg, hen 1.0 to 1.1 kg, yellow skin and legs, gold plumage and north-east Italian origin with Agraria.org, which draws on the Veneto Agricoltura CO.VA. project. FAO DAD-IS lists a white shell, 140 to 180 eggs and slightly heavier birds (1.5 and 1.2 kg); two sources agree on pinkish eggs, so that value stays. Added egg size small (40 to 45 g) and broodiness high (Agraria.org: marked tendency to brood and rear chicks).

Egg color changed from cream to light brown to white, the shell color in the official Italian (FIAV) standard printed by Agraria.org, which also describes good output of large 50 to 60 g white eggs; Wikipedia's cream to light brown kept as a conflicting alternative. Added egg size medium to large (50 to 60 g in both sources) and temperament lively, trusting (the standard: lively, ornamental, trusting character). Confirmed weights (cock 1.8 to 2.3 kg, hen 1.5 to 2.0 kg) with FAO DAD-IS (2.0 and 1.8 kg), and Italian origin with DAD-IS and Agraria.org.

Temperament curious, lively, trustful replaced with pleasant: Star Milling, the only source, says only that the birds have a pleasant personality. feathered_legs and crest changed from true to yes to match the value style used elsewhere. Star Milling gives 3 to 4 lb for the breed without splitting by sex, so hen 1.4 kg and rooster 1.8 kg are a reading of that range, not a stated figure. FAO DAD-IS (Pavlov, Russia) confirms Russian origin and a native at risk population of about 160 to 450 birds in 2025. White eggs, 70 to 90 a year, rest on Star Milling alone, so the record stays flagged.

Temperament active, hardy cut to active: hardy describes toughness, not temperament. cold_hardy cleared: Wikipedia says the birds resist disease and adverse environmental conditions, which does not state cold hardiness, and no other source covers it. Confirmed Portuguese origin, dual meat and egg use, fly-tying feather use and not at risk status with FAO DAD-IS (about 11,300 to 19,400 birds in 2026). Weights (cock 2.6 to 3.2 kg, hen 2.2 to 2.7 kg) rest on Wikipedia alone, and no source gives egg count, color or size, so the record stays flagged.

Egg color trimmed to dark brown (the darkest-egg note belongs in the text, not the field); Wikipedia and Star Milling both say very dark brown, and FAO DAD-IS says reddish. Added weights from the Wikipedia infobox, cock 2.3 to 3 kg and hen 1.7 to 2.3 kg; DAD-IS gives 2.5 and 2.0 kg, inside those ranges. Added egg size large (60 g eggs in Wikipedia and DAD-IS). Removed the notable trait claiming it is one of only two dark-egg breeds with the Marans, which no checked source states. Confirmed about 150 to 160 eggs a year and Catalan origin with DAD-IS.

Comb value red (type not specified) cleared: it is a color note, and no source names the comb type. Added egg size small (eggs of at least 40 g, Wikipedia). Confirmed weights (cock 0.8 kg, hen 0.6 kg), French origin around 1900, creation by Raymond Lecointre to brood pheasant eggs, the 1928 standard and true bantam status with FAO DAD-IS. The 130 creamy white eggs a year rest on Wikipedia alone, so the record stays flagged.

Temperament cleared: tough and responsive to the environment describe hardiness, not temperament, and no source describes temperament. Egg color burnt-cream colour changed to light brown: FAO DAD-IS says light brown and Wikipedia and Star Milling describe the burnt-cream shade of the same tint. Added egg size large (60 to 65 g in Wikipedia, 65 g in DAD-IS). Purpose eggs changed to dual: DAD-IS lists eggs and meat, and the birds are heavy (cock 4 to 4.5 kg). Confirmed weights with DAD-IS (4 and 2.5 kg) and Asturian origin with all three sources.

Added from FAO DAD-IS (Polbar, Poland): cock 2.5 kg, hen 2 kg, cream egg shells, single comb and egg use. Confirmed the 1946 origin, Laura Kaufman's Green-legged Partridge by Plymouth Rock cross and the single conservation flock (about 1,000 to 1,100 birds) with both Wikipedia and DAD-IS. DAD-IS gives about 160 eggs a year as an average only, so no range was added. The new egg and weight facts rest on DAD-IS alone, so the record stays flagged.

Confirmed against the official Italian (FIAV) standard reproduced by Agraria.org: rooster 2.5 to 2.8 kg, hen 1.8 to 2.1 kg, whitish eggs of at least 50 g, black and white varieties, small V-shaped comb, pure white earlobes, white skin, and a bird kept for tasty meat plus fair laying (dual purpose). The 150 eggs a year minimum comes from Wikipedia only; Agraria.org describes laying as fair without a number. No changes.

Confirmed purpose (dual), barred pattern, autosexing and South African origin against Wikipedia and a 2025 peer-reviewed review in Discover Animals (Springer). Added egg_color brown (both sources). Added hen and rooster weights from the Wikipedia infobox (3.6 kg and 4.2 kg); the Springer review gives much lighter weights (hens 2.1 kg, males about 3 to 4 kg), so the hen weight carries a conflict. The review dates the breed to the 1950s against Wikipedia's 1960s; left 1960s in place. Review reports about 196 to 198 eggs a year from one line of studies only, so no egg count was added. No source covers temperament or climate tolerance, so needs_review stays true.

Every filled field matches Wikipedia: dual purpose, black only with a blue-green sheen, single comb with five or six points, bright red earlobes, clean slate legs, cocks 2.5 to 3.0 kg and hens 1.7 to 2.5 kg, north-west Portugal, not at risk in 2024. The FAO DAD-IS record confirms Portugal as origin, not-at-risk status and meat plus egg use; the DGAV (Portuguese veterinary authority) page confirms it is an official native breed with a herdbook kept by AMIBA. No source found gives egg color, egg count, temperament or climate tolerance, so needs_review stays true.

Temperament was a list that mixed in a flight trait (friendly, strong flyer); replaced with friendly, docile (Wikipedia says friendly, The Featherbrain says docile). High broodiness confirmed by both. Small white eggs, crest, single comb with tassel, Mille Fleur pattern and northeastern US origin checked against Wikipedia. The Featherbrain lists origin as Europe, which matches the Dutch or Belgian ancestry Wikipedia gives, so the US origin stays. Egg color and size have only one publisher; the only other pages found were forums, so needs_review stays true.

Weights (hens 2.0 to 2.5 kg, cocks 2.5 to 3.0 kg), white or light cream eggs, dual purpose, white and buff colors, 1874 Hamburg debut and German origin all confirmed by the GEH (German rare breeds society) breed page. Egg count: Wikipedia gives about 170 a year and GEH about 150, so added eggs_per_year_min 150 alongside the existing max of 170. Added temperament lively, tame (GEH: spirited birds that become very tame with their keeper) and cold_hardy yes (GEH: good weather hardiness, known as a winter layer). Kept in review: some key facts have fewer than two publishers (strict rule).

Purpose dual-purpose to dual and autosexing true to yes, to match the field value styles. Egg color brown-tinted to light brown (Rare Breeds Survival Trust says light brown; Star Milling's brown tinted means the same). Egg count 180 to 200 confirmed by RBST. Weights (6 to 9 lb, stored as 2.7 and 4.1 kg) come only from Star Milling and were kept. Empty varieties with no source cleared. Added bantam_available yes (RBST: a very rare bantam exists). Origin at the University of British Columbia in the 1940s plus a later UK strain confirmed by RBST and the Poultry Club of Great Britain. No source covers temperament or climate tolerance and weights have one publisher, so needs_review stays true.

Egg count 160 to 170, pinkish (salmon) shells, dual purpose, yellow skin and legs, red earlobes, single comb and creation at the Rovigo poultry station from Buff Orpington and White America confirmed by Agraria.org, which reproduces the Veneto Agricoltura breed sheet. Rooster weight 3.8 to 4.0 kg: 3.8 was the bottom of the old ANSAV range (3.8 to 4.2 kg) while Veneto Agricoltura gives 4.0 to 4.5 kg; 4.0 sits inside both. Hen weight 2.8 kg fits both ranges and was kept. Added broodiness high (Agraria.org: strong urge to sit and rear chicks). Cleared the empty varieties field that had no source. Kept in review: some key facts have fewer than two publishers (strict rule).

Egg count 140 to 160, pinkish to brown shells, dual purpose, yellow skin and legs, red earlobes, single comb, silver-white plumage with dark spotting and creation at the Rovigo poultry station from Buff Orpington and White America confirmed by Agraria.org, which reproduces the Veneto Agricoltura breed sheet. Rooster weight 3.8 to 4.0 kg: 3.8 was the bottom of the old ANSAV range (3.8 to 4.2 kg) while Veneto Agricoltura gives 4.0 to 4.5 kg; 4.0 sits inside both. Hen weight 2.8 kg fits both ranges and was kept. Cleared the empty varieties field that had no source. Kept in review: some key facts have fewer than two publishers (strict rule).

Cleared cold_hardy yes: Wikipedia only says the young birds are hardy and fast growing, and Agraria.org speaks of general rusticity; neither says anything about cold. White eggs, single comb, cream earlobes sometimes tinged blue, mostly white skin, silver and golden black-flecked varieties and Emilia-Romagna origin confirmed by Agraria.org (breed sheet with the ARVAR draft standard). Egg count (about 150) and weights (cocks 2.0 to 2.5 kg, hens 1.9 to 2.0 kg) have only Wikipedia, so needs_review stays true.

Temperament was a list (friendly, alert) and the sources disagree on friendliness (Wikipedia says usually friendly with some aggressive cocks, Star Milling says docile but not friendly), so it is now the shared ground: alert, active. Purpose ornamental/exhibition conflict settled as exhibition; both sources say the breed is kept almost only for showing. Origin Britain/England conflict dropped, England sits inside Britain. Weights kept at 0.6 kg cock and 0.5 kg hen (Wikipedia, UK figures) with the Star Milling US figures of 26 oz (0.7 kg) and 22 oz (0.6 kg) as conflicting alternatives. Added egg size small (Star Milling: one tiny egg a week). Cream eggs, low broodiness, rose comb, white earlobes and black, blue and white as main colors confirmed.

Cleared egg_color brown: Wikipedia gives brown eggs only for the American Manx Rumpy (Persian Rumpless), a separate line made in 1958 from tail-less birds of supposed Iranian origin, not for the British Rumpless Game. Cleared the empty varieties field that had no source. Tail-less (no uropygium), hard feather, bantam and large fowl, and British origin confirmed by the Poultry Club of Great Britain, which says the breed probably arose as a genetic accident in Old English Game and is far more common as a bantam. Weights (cocks 2.3 to 2.7 kg, hens 1.8 to 2.3 kg) have only Wikipedia, and no source gives egg color, egg count or temperament, so needs_review stays true.

Purpose fighting/ornamental conflict settled as ornamental: Wikipedia says steel-spur fighting is no longer legal in Japan and the breed is now kept for fancy, and Aviculture-Europe describes it as a show breed today. Weights 3.4 kg cock and 2.6 kg hen confirmed within rounding by Aviculture-Europe (about 3.5 and 2.5 kg). Added broodiness high (Aviculture-Europe: hens are good broodies). Japanese origin in Kagoshima (old Satsuma province) and the 1943 protected designation confirmed. No source gives egg color, egg count or temperament. Kept in review: some key facts have fewer than two publishers (strict rule).

Weights (hens 2.4 to 2.8 kg, cocks 2.8 to 3.5 kg), dual purpose, white plumage with a frost-resistant red rose comb, cold hardiness, the 1905 origin and the near loss before the 1991 rescue confirmed by ProSpecieRara, the Swiss rare breeds foundation. Egg color tinted to cream: ProSpecieRara calls the eggs cream colored, sometimes with a faint lilac sheen, which is what Wikipedia's tinted means. ProSpecieRara gives about 120 eggs a year, the low end of the existing 120 to 200 range, which was kept. Added temperament calm, friendly (ProSpecieRara: calm and trusting birds that neither fly well nor like to). Cleared the empty varieties field that had no source.

Temperament was a one-item list; set to the plain string docile (Star Milling). Egg count: the old value was stored as a minimum of 180, but the Rare Breeds Survival Trust says up to 180 depending on strain and Wikipedia says about 180, so 180 moved to eggs_per_year_max and the minimum cleared. Added hen 2.7 kg and rooster 3.2 kg from the Scots Dumpy Club's copy of the British Poultry Standards (6 lb and 7 lb). White or cream eggs confirmed by RBST (white to tinted) and the club standard (white). High broodiness confirmed by the Poultry Club of Great Britain and Star Milling. Scottish origin, short legs from a dwarfing gene, bantam form and cuckoo, black and white colors confirmed. Kept in review: some key facts have fewer than two publishers (strict rule).

Low broodiness confirmed by the Rare Breeds Survival Trust (only very occasionally broody) and the Poultry Club of Great Britain (a non-sitting breed). Cold hardiness kept: RBST says the breed is known for hardiness and thrives in any climate. Added eggs_per_year_min 150 and eggs_per_year_max 180 (RBST). Added temperament alert, active (RBST, which also notes birds can be excitable and males feisty in the breeding season). Varieties set to barred, the only color (RBST), replacing an empty list with no source. Dual purpose, single comb, red earlobes, bantam form and Scottish origin confirmed. White eggs and the weights (7 lb cock, 5 lb hen) have only Wikipedia, so needs_review stays true.

Dual purpose and Indonesian origin (Ciamis, West Java) confirmed by the FAO DAD-IS record, which lists eggs, meat and hobby keeping and says the breed descends from red junglefowl long adapted to the Ciamis area. Added comb pea (some single) from DAD-IS, which says most birds have a pea comb and a share have single combs. Cleared the empty varieties field that had no source. No source found gives egg color, egg count, weights or temperament; the one Indonesian survey paper cited by Wikipedia returned 403, so needs_review stays true.

Egg count 180 to 180 widened to 140 to 180 (Livestock Conservancy; Star Milling says about 180). Egg size small to small to medium (Livestock Conservancy). Added egg_color white, hen 2.3 kg and rooster 2.9 kg (Livestock Conservancy: 5 lb and 6.5 lb). Temperament was a list (active, friendly, tame); set to active, can be flighty from the Livestock Conservancy, which says strains range from almost wild to docile, with Star Milling's friendly as a flagged alternative. Added broodiness low (non-broody), heat_tolerant yes and cold_hardy no (Livestock Conservancy: good for hot climates, dislikes cold). Cleared the empty varieties field. Egg purpose, cup comb, bantam form, Sicilian origin and the red (British) versus white (American) earlobe split confirmed.

Weight conflicts were only the two ends of one range, so they are now ranges: rooster 2.0 to 2.4 kg and hen 1.6 to 1.8 kg, matching the official Italian (FIAV) standard on Agraria.org. Added temperament lively, likes to roam and cold hardy partly from Agraria.org (a lively bird of roaming habit that copes fairly well with cold). Confirmed white to light brown elongated eggs of at least 45 g, egg-laying purpose, cup comb, red earlobes with some white allowed, yellow skin, willow-green legs, the four colors and North African ancestry against Agraria.org and FAO DAD-IS.

Merged isbar into this record: Wikipedia says the breed was known as Isbar, Blue Isbar and Swedish green egg layer until it was renamed Silverudd Blue in 2016, so silverudd-blue is the current name and isbar is now an alias. Folded in from isbar (Star Milling): about 200 eggs a year, cold hardy, egg purpose (Wikipedia's eggs and meat kept as a dual alternative), developed from the 1950s, green eggs, metallic hackles on cocks. Earlier checks kept: egg size medium to large from 50 to 65 g eggs, blue/green eggs, hen about 1.5 kg and cock about 2.5 kg, black, blue and splash, single comb, Swedish origin. Egg color and origin now agree across Wikipedia and Star Milling, but weights rest on Wikipedia alone and egg numbers and cold hardiness on Star Milling alone, so it stays flagged for review. Summary rewritten for the merged record.

Purpose dual to meat: Wikipedia classes it as a heavy meat breed used mainly for broilers, with laying only a secondary use. Autosexing yes cleared: the breed itself is not autosexing; only chicks from a cross with an early-feathering rooster can be sexed by feather speed, which the notable traits already say. Added egg size large (eggs about 60 g). Cleared the empty varieties list. Confirmed about 200 brown eggs a year, rooster 4.5 kg and hen 3.0 kg averages, white plumage, single comb, red earlobes, yellow skin, White Plymouth Rock origin around 1960 and the 2020 count of 340 birds. Only Wikipedia covers this breed, so it stays flagged for review.

Added the missing weights from Wikipedia: rooster 3.0 to 3.5 kg, hen 2.3 to 2.7 kg. Added egg size large (average egg about 59 g). Cleared the empty varieties list. Confirmed 240 to 250 light brown eggs a year, egg-laying purpose, single comb, red earlobes, 1970 start from Barred and White Plymouth Rock stock and Slovenian origin against Wikipedia; FAO DAD-IS lists the breed in Slovenia with eggs and crossbreeding as its uses. No second publisher found for weights or egg numbers, so it stays flagged for review.

Added the missing weights from Wikipedia: rooster 2.5 to 3.0 kg, hen 1.8 to 2.2 kg. Added egg size large (average egg about 61 g). Cleared the empty varieties list. Confirmed 295 to 305 brown eggs a year, egg-laying purpose, single comb, earlobe colors, 1970s development from Rhode Island Red stock and Slovenian origin against Wikipedia; FAO DAD-IS lists the breed in Slovenia with eggs and crossbreeding as its uses. No second publisher found for weights or egg numbers, so it stays flagged for review.

Added the missing weights from Wikipedia: rooster 2.7 to 3.2 kg, hen 2.2 to 2.4 kg. Added egg size large (average egg about 64 g) and yellow skin from the same article. Cleared the empty varieties list. Confirmed 260 to 270 brown eggs a year, egg-laying purpose, single comb, light red earlobes with white blotches and Slovenian origin against Wikipedia; FAO DAD-IS lists the breed in Slovenia with eggs and dam-line crossing as its uses. No second publisher found for the weights or egg figures, so it stays flagged for review.

Confirmed every filled field against Wikipedia: 200 to 220 eggs a year, dual purpose, crested, Serbia, early 20th century, history and traits all match. No second publisher found with breed facts (the FAO DAD-IS datasheet did not load and no record is linked), so needs_review stays true. Egg color, egg size and temperament are not stated by any source and stay empty.

Confirmed every filled field against Wikipedia: 215 to 220 brown eggs a year, Bulgaria, about 1970, critical SAVE status, traits and history all match. The FAO DAD-IS record confirms the Bulgarian origin, the Rhode Island Red cross and an at risk status, but gives no egg or weight figures. Only a forum repeats the laying figures, so the key facts rest on one publisher and needs_review stays true.

Confirmed the filled fields: 130 to 180 eggs a year and low broodiness (non-sitters) from Wikipedia, with Omlet giving about 160 a year; dual purpose, Austria, about 1900, varieties and history match Wikipedia, the Poultry Club of Great Britain and FAO DAD-IS. Added egg color cream to light brown (Wikipedia infobox, Omlet says cream), cold hardy yes (Omlet: copes with all weather; Poultry Club: hardy), temperament friendly, docile when handled (Omlet, which notes they can be flighty at first) and crest yes (Omlet: both sexes crested; DAD-IS: small tuft).

Weights fixed: Star Milling says birds weigh 5 to 8 pounds with no split by sex, but Wikipedia (Svarthona: roosters up to 2 kg, hens no more than 1.5 kg) and Greenfire Farms (roosters about 4 lb) agree the breed is small, so hen 2.3 kg to 1.5 kg and rooster 3.6 kg to 2.0 kg. Egg size set small (Wikipedia: 38 to 48 g). Temperament list replaced with friendly, relaxed (Greenfire Farms, Star Milling). Cold hardy set yes (Greenfire Farms).
